title: The eight curve assertions and restriction to a dense open
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure] of characteristic exponent $p$, let $X$ be a separated scheme of finite type over $k$ with $\dim X\le1$, and let $F$ be a torsion abelian sheaf on $X_{\Et}$ which is constructible [def-weil-pbc-constructible-torsion], so that $(X,F)$ is a curve coefficient pair [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting]. Let $j:X'\hookrightarrow X$ be the inclusion of a dense open subscheme, $j^{-1}F$ the restriction of $F$ to $X'$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and $j_!j^{-1}F$ its extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], again a torsion abelian sheaf on $X_{\Et}$. Let $\mathcal C(X,-)$ be the eight assertions of [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions], each read as an implication that holds when its hypotheses fail (Stacks, Situation 0A52: 'those statements that apply'). Then:
1. If $\mathcal C(X,j_!j^{-1}F)$ holds, then $\mathcal C(X,F)$ holds.
2. If $\mathcal C(X,F)$ holds and $F$ is $p$-primary or prime to $p$ [def-weil-pbc-primary-torsion] (in characteristic $0$ this is no condition; it holds whenever $F$ is killed by a prime number), then $\mathcal C(X,j_!j^{-1}F)$ holds.
In particular, for $F$ killed by a prime number, $\mathcal C(X,F)$ holds if and only if $\mathcal C(X,j_!j^{-1}F)$ holds.

proof.text: Apply the vanishing comparison to transport C1 and C2 using the additive equivalences in degrees greater than one, and transport C3 using its two conditional implications.

Transport C4 and C5 by the finiteness comparison and C6 and C7 by the base-change comparison. Transport C8 using the restriction equivalence. Assemble the eight fields with IsCurve.assertions_iff, first unconditionally from G to F and then from F to G under the torsion alternative.

For a sheaf killed by a prime r, coefficient conversion is additive and therefore preserves r times the identity being zero. The stalk fibre functor is additive, so every stalk element is killed by r. If r vanishes in k, CharP.charP_iff_prime_eq_zero makes F r-primary (power exponent one). Otherwise r is a unit in k and hence in the global sections of Spec k; this supplies the invertible-order torsion witness. Apply the reverse implication under this alternative and pair it with the forward implication to obtain the equivalence.

STATEMENT CORRECTED: the converse C(F)=>C(j_!j^{-1}F) is not derivable for (C3),(C4),(C6) when F mixes a p-primary and a prime-to-p part (e.g. F=j_!Z/l + i_*Z/p on an affine curve: C(X,F) says nothing about rho for j_!Z/l); part 2 now assumes F p-primary or prime to p, which holds in all three uses (sheaves killed by a prime). The 'again constructible' clause of the old statement is not needed by the proof and was dropped. Stacks 0GJA covers all eight assertions (1)-(8) = (C1)-(C8), each separately. No new nodes.

lean.statement: theorem IsCurve.dense_open_assertions {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (P : CurveCoefficientPair k) (hP : P.IsConstructible) (U : P.C.Opens) (hU : Dense (U : Set P.C)) : let E := (forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u + 1} ℤ) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).inv ⋙ ModuleCat.restrictScalars (ULift.ringEquiv : ULift.{u + 1} ℤ ≃+* ℤ).toRingHom let F := (sheafCompose P.C.smallEtaleTopology E).obj P.F let F' := (Etale.openImmersionLowerShriek AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} U.ι).obj ((Etale.upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} U.ι).obj P.F) let G := (sheafCompose P.C.smallEtaleTopology E).obj F' (IsCurve.Assertions (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ) P.toSpec G → IsCurve.Assertions (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ) P.toSpec F) ∧ ((Scheme.IsTorsionSheafOfInvertibleOrder (Spec (.of k)) F ∨ ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ CharP k p ∧ Scheme.IsPrimaryTorsionSheaf (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ) F p) → IsCurve.Assertions (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ) P.toSpec F → IsCurve.Assertions (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ) P.toSpec G) ∧ (∀ r : ℕ, r.Prime → r • 𝟙 P.F = 0 → (IsCurve.Assertions (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ) P.toSpec F ↔ IsCurve.Assertions (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ) P.toSpec G))
